evidence: app/src/app.js:214-231 — abilities route is one self-contained block
app/src/views.js:377-393 — abilityPage deletes cleanly
app/src/views.js:242-253 — Pokémon page Abilities section links to /abilities and must be edited separately
app/src/views.js:62,70 — pokemonCard 'hidden' option becomes dead code with the feature
app/public/styles.css:305 — .hidden-ability rule left orphaned
removability.rationale: Two source files and a stylesheet, but the feature leaks: the Pokémon page's Abilities section and the card component's hidden-ability support are separate edits, and removing the pages strands the typeEn variable and CSS.

evidence: app/src/views.js:62 — every card list funnels through pokemonCard, so the sprite fix is one place
app/src/api.js:81-84 — sprite/artwork URL construction centralized in the data module
app/src/views.js:181-185 — latest-flavor-text logic re-implemented inline despite latestEnglishFlavor existing (api.js:46)
app/src/views.js:180 — genus lookup inlined while englishGenus (api.js:42) is exported and unused
app/src/app.js:223-228 — ability route duplicates toSpeciesList's ref-to-species mapping (api.js:128-142)
changeability.rationale: Rendering-level fixes are one-place (single card component, single URL helper), but two data-shaping rules — flavor-text extraction and Pokémon-reference-to-species mapping — exist in two copies each, so those fixes must land twice.

evidence: app/src/api.js:3-6 — API base URL and cache known only to the api module
app/src/views.js:14-45 — every page goes through one layout; nav edits touch one function
app/public/app.js:1-7 — client JS is 8 lines of htmx config, fully separated from server code
app/src/views.js:10,160 — PAGE_SIZE (pagination policy) lives in the view module but is consumed by the router (app.js:66-70)
app/src/views.js:151 — typeEn passed as index.typeEn.get.bind(...) here, but as closures at views.js:186,349,379,426 — inconsistent seam
coupling.rationale: Layering is clean and views are pure functions of route-assembled data, but the typeEn lookup is threaded three different ways (often pointlessly — it is dead at views.js:379-392) and one routing policy constant lives on the wrong side of the seam.

evidence: app/src/views.js:136-158 — homeResults renders both the full page and the htmx fragment, avoiding a parallel partial template
app/src/views.js:309-343 — movesTable reused by the full page, the game-swap fragment, and the sort fragment (app.js:186-199)
app/src/views.js:82-87 — section()/cardGrid() give every page the same panel and card-list shape
app/src/views.js:62-76 — pokemonCard grows boolean flags (showTypes, hidden) and requires typeEn only conditionally
app/src/views.js:388-392 — abilityPage hand-rolls <ul class="cards"> instead of using cardGrid
abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the app's real variation well — fragment views double as htmx partials and the sort endpoint reuses the table renderer — with only minor flag creep and one bypassed helper.

findings.issue: Latest-English-flavor-text extraction is duplicated: latestEnglishFlavor exists in api.js:46-51 but pokemonPage re-implements it inline; englishGenus (api.js:42) is exported and never used, with the genus lookup inlined at views.js:180.
findings.suggestion: Delete the inline copies and call latestEnglishFlavor/englishGenus from pokemonPage (or drop the unused exports).

findings.issue: The ability route re-implements toSpeciesList's Pokémon-reference-to-species mapping (dedupe, alternate-form exclusion, dex ordering) just to attach a hidden flag, so changes to those rules must be made in two places.
findings.suggestion: Generalize toSpeciesList(refs, index, decorate) or have it return the matched ref alongside the species so the flag can be attached without duplicating the mapping.

findings.issue: The typeEn closure (n => index.typeEn.get(n) ?? humanize(n)) is defined five times (app.js:112; views.js:186,349,379,426) and threaded as an option through pokemonCard, where it is dead on the move and ability pages (views.js:368,388-392).
findings.suggestion: Export one typeEnglish(index, name) helper from api.js and drop the per-view closures and the dead threading.

findings.issue: PAGE_SIZE, a routing/pagination policy, is defined and re-exported from the view module (views.js:160) and imported by the router (app.js:66-70).
findings.suggestion: Move PAGE_SIZE into app.js next to the pagination logic.

findings.issue: serveStatic uses cwd-relative './public/...' paths, so npm start only works when run from app/; serving from any other directory 404s the stylesheet and htmx.
findings.suggestion: Resolve paths from import.meta.url (e.g. new URL('../public/styles.css', import.meta.url).pathname) or serve a root.

findings.issue: htmx.min.js is vendored into public/ while htmx.org is also a package.json dependency, so upgrading htmx requires remembering to re-copy.
findings.suggestion: Serve it straight from node_modules/htmx.org/dist/htmx.min.js, or drop the dependency.

findings.issue: abilityPage bypasses cardGrid and hand-rolls the same <ul class="cards"> markup, so a change to the card-list wrapper must be made twice.
findings.suggestion: Extend cardGrid to accept a per-item options mapper, or use cardGrid with the hidden flag folded into the species entry.

findings.issue: pokemonCard's typeEn option has no default but is only read when showTypes is true, so omitting it crashes at render time instead of degrading.
findings.suggestion: Default typeEn to a humanize-based fallback inside the component.

summary: This is a well-layered four-module app whose seams mostly line up with the features: one card component, one URL/cache module, one layout, and htmx fragments that reuse the full-page renderers. The costs are concentrated in a handful of half-used helpers — duplicated flavor-text and species-mapping logic, a typeEn lookup defined five ways, and a couple of constants and options on the wrong side of the seams. None of it would slow a maintainer down for long, but the duplications are exactly where the next data-rule change would land twice.

scenarios.notes: Card rendering is centralized but ordering is per-route (home app.js:56-71, move app.js:206, ability app.js:229, type app.js:245); home also needs sorting applied before slicing/pagination, and a sort control would repeat the URL-param plumbing home already has.
